_comment: 5E skillsets, structured — the profession half of a Low Powered build (25 of its 250).
Authored from the legacy prose in skillsets.json, which stated a list of name strings and a
hand-typed cost of 25.
As with the powersets and complications, NO cost is stated here: a skill carries its basecost
on the trait and the engine prices it. The prose's 'skills' is a catch-all over several .hdc
buckets -- skills, perks, talents -- so `buckets` may carry any of them.
HITTING 25 (Phil's rules). A set's listed skills rarely land on it. The levers:
Familiarity   1   roll becomes a flat 8-
Proficiency   2   roll becomes a flat 10-
Full skill    3   the normal roll
levels on a skill  +2 each, +1 to that skill's roll
Familiarity and Proficiency are what make an ODD remainder closable -- `levels` alone moves in
2s. Each set's `note` records what it needed.
Skill levels go in the `skill` array itself, NOT a `skillLevels` sub-key: unlike powers,
nothing folds a skills sub-key in. populateTrait reads only `skill` and `list`, plus the skill
ENHANCERS (linguist, scientist, scholar...) which it pushes in by name. A skillLevels sub-key
is silently dropped, costing 0 rather than erroring.
SKILL_LEVELS is a level across SEVERAL skills, priced by option: CHARACTERISTIC 2,
SINGLEMOVEMENT 2, ALLMOVEMENT 3, RELATED 3 ('any three related Skills'), SIMILAR 5 ('a group
of similar Skills'), NONCOMBAT 8, OVERALL 10. A level in ONE skill is that skill's own
`levels`, at 2 apiece.
'Player Defined' is deliberate, not a placeholder: the prose's 'Lang:' and 'SS[INT]:' named no
language and no science, so the player names their own. These are the fields the
editable-fields work should reach first.
A skill needs its `characteristic` (PRE, INT, DEX...) or it has NO ROLL -- the sheet shows the
skill with a blank roll rather than erroring. levelsonly: false is the default.
See docs/RANDOM_CHARACTER.md. Verified in core/random/__tests__/skillset.test.ts -- every set
must total exactly 25.

skillsets.note: Its seven skills at 3 plus 'SL: Interactive Skills +1' — a group level, SIMILAR at 5 — come to 26, one over. Seduction is dropped to a Proficiency (2, a flat 10- roll) to land on 25: an odd remainder, so `levels` (+2 steps) could not close it. Seduction is the least load-bearing of the seven for this profession.
